cultivar: Qing Xin Oolong, TTES No. 12 (Jin Xuan)
processing: Lightly oxidised and semi-ball rolled with little or no roast, typical of Taiwanese high-mountain oolong.
harvest_season: Spring is the usual main picking for high-mountain oolong, with winter lots also common in central Taiwan.
appearance_dry: Tight deep-green semi-rolled balls, typical of high-mountain oolong.
appearance_liquor: Pale clear yellow-green, typical of high-mountain oolong.
appearance_wet: Thick green leaves that open fully, typical of the class.
taste_profile: As with other high-mountain oolongs, expect floral sweetness and a soft body with low bitterness; lots at the lower end of the altitude range are lighter.

brewing.notes: Hot water and a long opening steep; keep later steeps shorter.

vintage_note: Usually sold by harvest of the current year and drunk fresh within a year or so, as with other unroasted Taiwanese high-mountain tea. Ask which garden and which season, since the name covers a wide range of altitudes.
description:
Yu Shan oolong comes from the Yushan tea area in Xinyi Township, Nantou, in the foothills below Taiwan's highest peak. Caopingtou is the tea place usually mentioned. The mountain itself is far higher than the gardens: Caopingtou sits at about 1,300 metres.

The usual cultivars are Qing Xin Oolong and Jin Xuan, made in the light rolled style. Cool, misty conditions are the reason given for the tea's quality, in line with other high-mountain districts.

Expect the familiar high-mountain character, floral, sweet and smooth, with less weight than the highest-altitude teas. Brew it hot, and give the leaf room to open.

The Yu Shan name sounds grander than some of the gardens are, so look past the label. Ask where the garden sits and which harvest it is; a garden near 1,300 metres is a perfectly good tea, but it should not be priced like a Lishan.
history: Little is documented on when tea came to this part of Xinyi. Caopingtou in Tongfu village, known for its Yushan oolong, has since also become a tourist tea garden, known for winter cherry blossom.
